Subject: Re: Intro / discovery — hosted API traffic + pricing follow-up

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can put together a clean hosted pricing recommendation for Southbridge.

Recap of what I captured on the call:
- Primary workload: conversational assistant + summary extraction for clinician notes.
- Expected production ramp window: next 6–9 months.
- Current integration: all tokens flow through hosted API (no edge caching yet).

As we discussed, to model a price band and recommend commit vs pay-as-you-go we need confirmation on two things: monthly token volume and peak TPS characteristics. From the conversation I logged the following tentative numbers — can you confirm or correct?

- Expected average monthly tokens: 25–40M (you mentioned mid-30s)
- Budget target: ~$18–$22 per 1M tokens (goal $/1M to fit procurement constraints)
- Peak TPS: sustained bursts ~200–250 TPS for 3–5 minutes, transient spikes up to ~400 TPS for short windows

If those are accurate we’ll run two hosted scenarios: (A) pay-as-you-go at standard hosted bands and (B) 12-month reserved slab with burst capacity — we’ll show the unit economics and monthly burn for both. Marissa will include quantization/latency tradeoffs that could lower the $/1M.

Next steps from our side: I’ll share a short pricing note + recommended slabs after you confirm the numbers and send the monthly traffic snapshot you referenced. I attached the Redwood_Hosted_Pricing_Guide_v2.pdf for reference (high level pricing bands + examples).

Your asks for us: please confirm the monthly tokens range, confirm expected sustained burst duration, and attach the usage profile you mentioned. Also flag if you need an SLA or data residency requirement called out explicitly in the proposal — those change pricing and lead time.

Proposed meeting to review pricing: Wed 6/9 10:00am PT (30 mins) — does that work?

Thanks,

On Mon, 7 Jun 2027 at 15:12, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Expected average monthly tokens: 25–40M (you mentioned mid-30s)

This is correct as an average — our internal forecast is ~32M tokens/month for Q3, with month-to-month variability of 20–50M depending on pilot uptake.

> - Budget target: ~$18–$22 per 1M tokens (goal $/1M to fit procurement constraints)

Procurement is targeting $20/1M as a ceiling for the hosted option. If you can show committed slabs that push that to $16–$18/1M we’ll prioritize that route.

> - Peak TPS: sustained bursts ~200–250 TPS for 3–5 minutes, transient spikes up to ~400 TPS for short windows

Realistic peak guidance: sustained (user-driven) bursts ~220 TPS for 3–5 minutes is our base case. During coordinated push (end-of-shift syncs) we can get to ~420 TPS for 20–60 seconds. We don’t currently have buffering — that’s something we’ll discuss.

- Does the hosted price include KV-prefix caching / small request cache? Any guidance on token savings we could expect from prefix caching?
- We will need basic SOC2 evidence (scope) and a note in the contract about data retention — I’ll route the security contacts if required.

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed snapshot, that was helpful. A few clarifications from pricing/solutions that will materially change the $/1M we model: 

1) Caching & request shape: if you can enable prefix-level caching for repeated system prompts and reuse the KV cache for chat sessions, we generally see 10–25% token savings for conversation-heavy flows. The exact uplift depends on average sequence length; I ran a quick back-of-envelope on your file and put a conservative 12% token-savings number in the attached hosted-pricing-slabs.csv.

2) Burst sizing: for hosted API we can handle 420 TPS transient spikes but price and capacity depend on whether you want guaranteed burst vs best-effort. Guaranteed burst via reserved slab + burst cushion locks capacity and reduces per-1M price. Example: a 12-month reserved slab at 30M tokens/month with a burst cushion reduces $/1M by ~15% vs pay-as-you-go. I added two worked scenarios in the attached CSV.

3) SLA & security: basic hosted plan includes SOC2 type II summary and standard data retention defaults (30 days retention for logs, customer data retention configurable). If you need an explicit SLA (99.9% with uptime credits) or data residency (customer VPC), that typically moves you to Dedicated or Private and requires a different pricing model — I flagged those rows in the sheet.

Proposed near-term artifacts I’ll send before our Wed meeting:
- Short pricing note (2–3 pages) with the two scenarios: pay-as-you-go and 12-month reserved slab (with burst cushion).
- A worked example showing $/1M, monthly $ burn, and expected latency tradeoffs with quantized model variants.

Can you confirm which of the two you prefer we show first in the worksheet (1) pay-as-you-go baseline, or (2) 12-month committed slab with burst cushion? We’ll prioritize accordingly for the 6/9 10:00 PT call.
